subject: Discovery recap + checklist: streaming UX & concurrency for CloudVision
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>
To: Anna Kim <anna.kim@cloudvision.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-10-18T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Discovery recap + checklist: streaming UX & concurrency for CloudVision

Anna — great to meet today, and thanks to Paul for joining. Quick recap of what we heard and a short checklist to keep the POC moving. Please reply inline if anything below is off.

Key pain points (what you told us)
- Chat UX suffers from long first-block delays; users expect token-by-token streaming for assistant replies.
- 95th-percentile latency spikes under load, particularly during peak business hours and concurrent sessions.
- Current cost for higher concurrency is pushing the infra team to limit parallel sessions; this impacts customer experience for larger orgs.

Current stack (as described)
- Inference: in-house GPU pool behind REST endpoints (K8s + Istio), variant routing through a Python API layer.
- Proxy/edge: Nginx + CloudFront for static assets.
- Observability: homegrown metrics (Prometheus) and logs (ELK); limited token-level traces.

Success criteria for a successful POC / pilot
1) Streaming UX: first byte within 150–300ms and consistent token streaming (no 2–3s stalls) for 90% of conversations.
2) Latency SLA: p95 for full response (up to 256 tokens) < 400ms under stated concurrency profile.
3) Concurrency throughput: sustain 350 concurrent chat sessions with median latency under target and graceful degradation for bursts to 600 concurrent sessions.
4) Measurable cost comparison: projected token cost reduction or equivalent cost-neutral performance improvement.

Immediate asks / checklist for CloudVision (what we need from you)
- Small telemetry dump: 6 hours of representative traffic (Prometheus + example request/response pairs, truncated where needed) — we can accept a link to a Drive file.
- Concurrency profile: typical sessions per minute, average session length (messages / tokens), and 95th-percentile spikes (times of day).
- Sample prompt sizes and maximum response token lengths you expect for the chat UX.
- Any redlines on security / networking (VPC peering, IP allowlist) for a short-term POC.

Our proposed next steps
1) We’ll prepare a short POC proposal (2-week technical run) with proposed topology (hosted + isolated pool or Dedicated suggestion). Target delivery: internal draft by Fri 10/23.
2) Redwood eng will run a quick perf baseline with your telemetry and provide a config for streaming + batching.
3) Schedule a 30-minute sync with your infra lead (Paul) to align on network and auth for the POC — can we aim for Mon 10/19?

Attachments: I’ve attached a sketch of your current topology (cloudvision-current-topology.png) and the call recording. I’ve also included a small example telemetry file to show the format we need.

Thanks again — excited to work with you to get streaming working smoothly.

—
Logan Wright
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
logan.wright@redwoodinference.com | +1 415-555-0182

From: Anna Kim <anna.kim@cloudvision.ai>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Paul Ortiz <paul.ortiz@cloudvision.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-10-19T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Discovery recap + checklist: streaming UX & concurrency for CloudVision

Thanks Logan — appreciate the concise recap. A few quick notes inline and answers to the checklist items.

> Small telemetry dump: 6 hours of representative traffic
We can share a 6-hour window from last Tuesday (09:00–15:00 PT). I’ll put the export on Drive (link below) with sensitive fields redacted. The export will include Prometheus time-series, example requests, and some sampling of responses (truncated).

> Concurrency profile: typical sessions per minute, average session length
Typical: 180–220 concurrent sessions outside peak. Peak: observed short spikes up to ~580 concurrent sessions for 10–12 minute windows, notably during customer demo windows. Average session length: ~4 messages/user; avg response target ~140 tokens.

> Sample prompt sizes and max response tokens
Prompts vary: median ~60 tokens; 90th percentile ~180 tokens. Max response token length we currently cap at 512 for the assistant, but typical responses for UI flows are <256 tokens.

> Security/networking
We prefer VPC peering for any dedicated POC environment. We’ll need an NDA + data processing addendum before exporting non-anonymized logs. Our security team will share a short questionnaire.

We’ll upload the telemetry and the network contact for Paul by EOD 10/19. Mon 10/19 for a short sync is tight for us — can we do Tue 10/20 at 10:00 PT instead? Paul will join.

Link: https://drive.company/shared/CloudVision-Discovery-20261018 (I will update permissions).

—
Anna Kim
Head of Product, CloudVision
anna.kim@cloudvision.ai

Date: 2026-10-20T09:17:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: CloudVision POC next steps (engineer assignments + ask list)

Marissa / Monica — quick internal note following Anna’s confirmation.

Summary of commitments from CloudVision
- Telemetry export (6 hours) available on Drive; security questionnaire and NDA required before unredacted export.
- Concurrency: baseline 180–220 concurrent, spikes to ~580, avg response ~140 tokens, cap at 512 tokens.

Immediate internal actions
1) Marissa: please own the POC config doc and proposed topology. I suggest we present two options: (A) hosted isolated pool with token-level caching + streaming tuned kernels, (B) Redwood Dedicated (reserved capacity) with autoscale headroom to cover 600-concurrency bursts. Draft due Wed 10/21 COB.
2) Monica: can you scope a lightweight benchmarking harness (k6 + token-stream simulator) that mirrors their session distribution? Need baseline runs with current default serving kernel and then our optimized streaming path. Target: first runs by Thu 10/22.
3) I’ll prepare the POC SOW and a short security note about VPC peering + DPA. Also drafting the cost comparison model for both options.

Risk notes / questions for the call
- If their telemetry indicates heavy long-response (>=400 tokens) use, we need to flag memory/KV cache pressure and propose a quantization/segment approach.
- Their preference for VPC peering means we’ll need networking docs and an infra kickoff with our infra team; plan for a half-day setup window.

I’ll schedule the Tue 10/20 10:00 PT sync with Anna + Paul and loop in eng infra (TBD). Any objections?

—
Logan Wright
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
